CheckTitle: Vercel project is linked to a Git repository so deployments are traceable to commits
Description: **Vercel projects** are assessed for a **Git repository link**. A linked project deploys from commits pushed to GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, so each deployment maps to a reviewed commit; an unlinked project only receives deployments uploaded with the Vercel CLI from an arbitrary machine.
Risk: Without a Git link, anyone holding a Vercel token can deploy **unreviewed code** straight to production from a laptop, bypassing branch protection, pull request review and CI. There is no commit to audit, so a **malicious or compromised deployment** is hard to detect and roll back, and supply-chain controls on the repository do not apply to what is actually served.

Code.Other:
1. Navigate to your Vercel project dashboard
2. Go to Settings > Git
3. Click Connect Git Repository and choose the GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket repository that holds the project source
4. Set the Production Branch to the protected branch
5. Remove CLI-based deployment tokens that are no longer needed

Recommendation.Text:
Deploy every project from a **linked Git repository** with a protected production branch.
- Keep pull request review and CI as the only path to production
- Limit Vercel tokens that can run `vercel deploy --prod`
- Enable Git fork protection and deployment protection on the linked project
